convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? At night I cry quietly so no one hears. Gotta keep moving."
James has an edge today — something curdled.
"This one — Soursop. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Lily of the Valley. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what they confided."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Alejandra owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Alejandra said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then James grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"I sleep in shifts now — two hours, up, listen, two more. My body learned it before my head agreed. Chengdu, China never taught me that. The treeline did."
"Still on how you slept."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Since Alejandra died... I keep expecting to see Alejandra at the fire. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Wei is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I rinse the cup twice. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Alejandra's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Wild Ginger — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
James: "Don't just stand there — you've got opinions, right?"
"This one — Chinese Chive. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Bamboo Shoot. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I dreamed Alejandra was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
They give you the benefit of the doubt. This time.
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Seen worse."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Alejandra always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Wei is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them American Hazelnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Onni. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I wasn't a journalist. I was a chimney sweep. I wasn't protecting myself. I was protecting someone else."
"That again?" Onni sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"We went over this," Onni says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"We lost Christian, James, Bárbara, Desmond, Wei, Daniyar, Naran and Valeria. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"With you leading? ...Give me a day to think."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"It keeps getting worse. I can't haul or hunt with it like this — and if it festers, I'm done for. Please, clean it out and bind it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Valeria always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Ava has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Wei nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I greet everyone by name each morning. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Alejandra is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer.
d41: 🕯️ Alejandra Ramos is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Alejandra kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Alejandra's gone." James looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Alejandra." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Christian blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Camp Cooking (Level 1). Cooking uses half the water, +10% kcal. Once per day: add a Secret Ingredient (a random inventory item) — 50% delicious (+morale), 50% educational.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.

d41: The warm hum behind your ribs is gone. The reactor went with Alejandra's body — it does not come out, and it does not pass on. Hunger is back on the table. (One reactor per world, and the world already spent its one.)
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"

d41: The fire knew Christian before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
